intended_object: The canonical inclusion I ↪ R of a two-sided ideal into its ring, viewed as a non-unital ℤ-algebra homomorphism (non-unital ring homomorphism). Taken from the docstring; it is used to build the map Unitization ℤ I → R, (z, i) ↦ z + i.
explanation: The map sends x to its underlying element x.1, so it is the inclusion, and the zero, addition, multiplication and ℤ-scalar fields all hold by rfl. That matches the docstring. Mathlib's `TwoSidedIdeal.subtype` is only the same inclusion as an R-linear map; Mathlib has no version of it as a non-unital algebra hom, which is the form needed here to apply `NonUnitalAlgHom.toAlgHom` and lift the map to `Unitization ℤ I`. The base ring ℤ is the natural choice, because the unitization used in this file is over ℤ. The definition assumes `[Ring R]` where `[NonUnitalRing R]` would also work, but that is a trivial point in a library about general linear groups over unital rings, and the definition is not too narrow in any meaningful sense. It is a small helper map, but it is the standard canonical inclusion and is correctly formalized.
